title: Grade 5 Social Studies — Causes and Consequences of the American Revolution
subject: Social Studies
description: Practice with questions on taxation, independence, alliances, primary sources.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: What did many colonists mean by “no taxation without representation”?
choices: They wanted to end all elections in the colonies.
They wanted taxes set only by France.
They objected to taxes passed by a legislature in which they had no elected representatives.
They claimed there were no merchants to tax.

questions.question: What did the Stamp Act tax?
choices: only ocean water
many printed materials and legal papers
only farm-grown apples
all shoes from Mexico

questions.question: Why did protesters dump tea into Boston Harbor in 1773?
choices: to open a shipping business
to celebrate a completed peace treaty
to raise money for a tea shop
to oppose British tea policy and taxation

questions.question: Where did the first battles of the Revolutionary War take place in 1775?
choices: Detroit and New Orleans
Lexington and Concord
Jamestown and Plymouth
Yorktown and Paris

questions.question: What did the Declaration of Independence announce?
choices: The war was already over.
The colonies asked to join Parliament.
The colonies declared loyalty to France.
The colonies claimed to be independent states.

questions.question: When did the Continental Congress adopt the Declaration of Independence?
Who served as commander in chief of the Continental Army?
choices: Benjamin Franklin
Thomas Jefferson
George Washington
King George III

questions.question: Which people wanted the colonies to remain part of Britain?
choices: Loyalists
members of every Native nation
Patriots as a group
French soldiers

questions.question: Which country formally allied with the United States in 1778?
choices: Germany
Britain
France
Canada

questions.question: What agreement formally ended the war between Britain and the United States in 1783?
choices: U.S. Constitution
Treaty of Paris
Stamp Act
Mayflower Compact

questions.question: Which event came before Britain agreed to peace in 1783?
choices: The Louisiana Purchase was completed.
British forces surrendered at Yorktown.
Ohio became a state.
The U.S. Constitution was written in 1787.

questions.question: Why might a merchant stop buying goods from Britain before the war?
choices: to join a boycott in protest of British policies
to support higher taxes on the same goods
to vote in British Parliament
to make those goods cheaper in Britain directly

questions.question: Which source could show how one Loyalist described the conflict?
choices: a recent map with no comments
a modern price label for tea
a fictional story about a future election
a letter written by a Loyalist during the war

questions.question: Why were perspectives in the colonies different during the Revolution?
choices: All Patriots wanted Britain to keep ruling.
No one knew which side their leaders chose.
People had different loyalties and risks.
Everyone had equal rights and agreed on what to do.

questions.question: What goal did the Declaration express even though many people were still enslaved?
choices: the end of all government
the claim that slavery had already ended everywhere
a ban on all writing
the ideal that people have equal rights

questions.question: Why did some enslaved people seek freedom through wartime service or escape?
choices: They were trying to gain liberty for themselves and their families.
They already had the same legal freedom as everyone else.
They were required to pay taxes as members of Parliament.
All armies promised safety and freedom to everyone.

questions.question: Why did some Native nations make alliances during the war?
choices: They all wanted the new states to expand onto their lands.
To protect their lands and interests in a changing conflict.
They had no lands or governments to protect.
All Native nations made the same choice together.

questions.question: What did a battle map help military leaders decide?
choices: where to move troops and supplies
the price of tea in every town
what each soldier thought
who would write all future laws

questions.question: How did French support help the Americans at Yorktown?
choices: French representatives wrote Britain's surrender before the battle began.
France fought for Britain at Yorktown.
French ships and troops helped block and pressure British forces.
French ships stopped American troops from reaching the area.

questions.question: Which timeline is in the correct order?
choices: Boston Tea Party → Declaration of Independence → Treaty of Paris
Declaration of Independence → Boston Tea Party → Treaty of Paris
Declaration of Independence → Treaty of Paris → Boston Tea Party
Treaty of Paris → Boston Tea Party → Declaration of Independence
